blocks.x: Claims triage in minutes, 55% faster cycle times with document intelligence

A top-5 global P&C insurer: a Insurance & Risk program run on the outcome-linked model with a blended Achala IT Solutions team. The name stays behind the NDA; the numbers are published with permission.
FNOL packets, estimates and medical files arrived unstructured; triage queues held claims for days.
Straight-through rates below 20% on simple claims; adjusters spent time typing, not deciding. Fraud signals arrived after settlement; SIU capacity wasted on low-value leads.

We deployed the claims decision pipeline: document intelligence (classification, extraction, validation) feeding EEMS Platform decision policies with confidence-threshold routing, network fraud analytics scoring claims pre-settlement, and a portfolio lakehouse unifying exposure and claims for steering. Adjusters work a review queue of pre-assembled cases with citations.

items: the agents ran inside a defined policy limit with replay, so autonomy never outran the evidence.
the models and retrieval systems were evaluated before anyone trusted them, grounded answers, cited sources, measured quality.
lineage and freshness were design constraints from week one, so the measurement never became the controversy.

blocks.x: The pattern behind the top-5 global P&C insurer program travels; the estate does not. Teams considering this path should expect the diagnostic to reshape scope at least once, that is the process working, not failing The engagement model here was outcome-linked; the same pattern runs fixed-scope where the estate allows it.
